deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. Folio 115v holds a pencil draft, heavily corrected, of a private letter from Riemann to his family. It survives on the back of sheets used for his natural-philosophy drafts: the 'Geistesmasse' fragments on the previous page, and on the next page the velocity potential with div v = 0 outside matter and = mu inside.

Content in modern German paraphrase: 'You have given me a really great joy and surprise with your dear letter [or tokens] and the presents, which arrived here on the second feast day [i.e. 26 December, or Easter/Whit Monday]. The [linen/shirts] came very conveniently; I had not counted on it at all, since I know how rarely you have had it [such things] in Q. [very probably Quickborn, his father's parish] at this time. The apples turned out quite excellent this year and kept very well despite the transport. Thanks to the remembrance of you, they have [graced] many a lunch table [of mine].'

The draft breaks off at 'Mittagstisch'. No formulas, computations or scientific claims appear. The page is biographically relevant only: it shows Riemann drafting family letters on the same paper stock as his Naturphilosophie notes, which may help date that bundle. This is a dating suggestion, not a certainty.

results.what: Draft of a private thank-you letter to family (gifts, linen, apples after a holiday)

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains only a personal letter draft with no mathematical or scientific content. Riemann's family correspondence (gifts sent from Quickborn and similar) is well documented in his biography.
transcription_corrections: 'durch Euren lieben Besuch[?]' is probably 'lieben Brief[e]' (or a similar word such as 'Zeichen'), since the presents 'arrived' by post; a visit does not fit the context.
'zu ...[?] geschickt habt' more likely reads 'in Q. gehabt habt' or 'zu Q. ...'; 'Q.' is plausibly Quickborn, where Riemann's father was pastor.
'zu[?] diesem Jahr' should read 'in diesem Jahr'.
'{+Wäsche+}' appears to be a corrected word ending in '-wäsche' or 'Hemden' after an interlinear 'meine ...'; the reading is uncertain.
The interlinear insertion before 'Mittagstisch' reads roughly 'durch die Erinnerung an Euch' and is placed above 'haben mir'; it is followed by 'manche an meinem Mittagstisch' (sentence unfinished).
The superscript 'zu erwarten' above line 1 belongs to a reworking of the opening phrase (e.g. 'ohne es zu erwarten').
